rule: Every visible pixel comes from fetched real game graphics (pret decompilation repos). Only cropping, tile placement per the games' own OAM/frame data, documented flips, position offsets, palette application, backdrop color, and 8x NEAREST upscaling were performed. No pixels were drawn or synthesized.

ref-party-icon-pulse.gif.element: Party-menu Pokémon icon, the continuous 2-frame healthy-state loop (Pikachu)

sources.note: 32x64 indexed PNG: two 32x32 frames stacked vertically

ref-party-icon-pulse.gif.cadence_basis: pokeemerald src/pokemon_icon.c sAnim_0: ANIMCMD_FRAME(0, 6), ANIMCMD_FRAME(1, 6) — 6 ticks at the GBA's ~59.7275 Hz ≈ 100.4 ms per frame (the full-HP cadence)

ref-textbox-arrow-bob.gif.element: Message-box down-arrow (▼) vertical bob — motion, not blink
ref-textbox-arrow-bob.gif.cadence_basis: pokeemerald src/text.c: sDownArrowYCoords[] = {0, 1, 2, 1}, delay 8 ticks ≈ 133.9 ms per step (533 ms period)

ref-coin-spin.gif.element: Duel coin toss — the full 8-step spin cycle (face → edge → face), metasprite-assembled tile by tile from the game's own frame table

sources.note: AnimData167 sequence (frames 0,1,2,3,4,5,2,6 held 4 ticks each) and AnimFrameTable79 OAM placements (y, x, tile, xflip/yflip) used verbatim

ref-coin-spin.gif.cadence_basis: poketcg anims3.asm AnimData167: each frame held 4 ticks ≈ 67 ms at ~59.7 Hz

ref-item-get-bounce.gif.element: Poké Ball open + sparkle presentation (item-get / release idiom): closed → opening → open, then the field sparkle plays its real 4-frame cycle above the ball

sources.note: 96x16 sheet of six 16x16 cells; sparkle pixels are palette index 14 = pure white, so the backdrop is a dark neutral (96,112,96) to keep them visible — in-game they draw over the overworld scene

ref-item-get-bounce.gif.cadence_basis: pokeemerald src/pokeball.c ball-open AnimCmd steps at 5 ticks ≈ 84 ms; sparkle cells held ~100 ms (6-cell one-shot cycle, middle 4 cells used)

ref-status-flash.gif.element: Battle status-condition badge (PSN) in a binary on/off alert blink

sources.note: 32x8 PSN strip from the stacked status-icon sheet

ref-status-flash.gif.cadence_basis: Badge art is real Emerald data; in-game the badge itself is static — the on/off blink is the era's binary alert idiom (era corpus §2: 100–250 ms on/off cycling, nothing eases), applied at the textbox 8-tick quantum (134 ms)

skipped.ref-card-flip.gif: No real flip frames obtainable: poketcg's card animations (anims3.asm AnimData158–163) are shuffle translations, not flips, and The Spriters Resource sheet downloads were not fetchable. Nothing was fabricated.
